variables.name: color/fg/on-accent

variables.name: color/border/default
variables.description: Separators and the outline of cards, panels and table cells. Not the only cue that identifies a control (it is below 3:1): use color.border.strong.

variables.name: color/border/strong
variables.description: The outline that identifies a control: inputs, checkboxes, outlined buttons (at least 3:1). Not for separators between content: use color.border.default.

variables.name: color/border/focus
variables.description: The border of a focused input, where the ring is drawn as the border itself. Not the outline drawn around a focused element: use ring.color with ring.width.

variables.name: color/ring
variables.description: The focus ring of any focusable element. Not a decorative border and not a selection colour: use color.interactive.selected.

variables.name: color/accent/fg
variables.description: Text and icons on color.accent.bg and its hover and pressed colours (the same colour as color.fg.on-accent). Not on color.accent.subtle-bg: use color.accent.subtle-fg.

variables.name: color/accent/bg
variables.description: The filled background of the primary action and of checked controls. Not for large areas, and not more than one primary action per view.

variables.name: color/accent/bg-hover
variables.description: color.accent.bg while hovered. Not a resting colour.

variables.name: color/accent/bg-active
variables.description: color.accent.bg while pressed. Not a resting colour.

variables.name: color/accent/subtle-bg
variables.description: A tinted background for accent badges, tags and highlighted callouts. Not for the selected row or item: use color.interactive.selected.

variables.name: color/accent/subtle-fg
variables.description: Text and icons on color.accent.subtle-bg. Not on color.accent.bg: use color.accent.fg.

variables.name: color/neutral/bg
variables.description: The filled background of a neutral action: a secondary solid button, a neutral badge. Not for the primary action: use color.accent.bg. Not for cards: use color.bg.surface.

variables.name: color/neutral/bg-hover
variables.description: color.neutral.bg while hovered. Not a resting colour.

variables.name: color/neutral/bg-active
variables.description: color.neutral.bg while pressed. Not a resting colour.

variables.name: color/neutral/fg
variables.description: Text and icons on color.neutral.bg and its hover and pressed colours. Not on a plain surface: use color.fg.default.

variables.name: color/neutral/subtle-bg
variables.description: A grey tinted background for neutral badges, tags and callouts. Not for a recessed area: use color.bg.inset.

variables.name: color/neutral/subtle-fg
variables.description: Text and icons on color.neutral.subtle-bg. Not on color.neutral.bg: use color.neutral.fg.

variables.name: color/interactive/hover
variables.description: A translucent wash over any background for hovered rows, menu items and ghost buttons. Not for filled controls: use the role's own hover token (color.accent.bg-hover).

variables.name: color/interactive/active
variables.description: The same wash while pressed. Not for a persistent selected state: use color.interactive.selected.

variables.name: color/interactive/selected
variables.description: A translucent accent wash for the selected row, item or tab. Not for hover, and not for text selection inside an editor.

variables.name: color/interactive/selected-hover
variables.description: The selected wash while the pointer is over the selected row, item or tab. Not for an unselected item: use color.interactive.hover.

variables.name: color/interactive/drag
variables.description: A translucent wash, in the blue ramp so it stays apart from selection, for an item being dragged and for the drop target it is over. Not for selection or hover.

variables.name: color/status/danger/solid
variables.description: The filled background of a destructive action, and the border of an invalid field. Not for danger text on a neutral background: use color.status.danger.fg.

variables.name: color/status/danger/solid-hover
variables.description: color.status.danger.solid while hovered. Not a resting colour.

variables.name: color/status/danger/solid-fg
variables.description: Text and icons on color.status.danger.solid and its hover colour. It is the ramp's own contrast colour, so it is white or dark ink as that solid needs. Not on a tinted status background: use the status fg. Not color.fg.on-accent, which belongs to the accent ramp.

variables.name: color/status/danger/fg
variables.description: Text and icons for errors and destructive actions, on neutral backgrounds or on color.status.danger.bg. Not the only signal: pair it with an icon or text, colour alone does not carry meaning.

variables.name: color/status/danger/bg
variables.description: A tinted background for errors and destructive actions: alerts, badges, inline messages. Not for filled buttons: use the status solid.

variables.name: color/status/danger/border
variables.description: The outline of a danger alert or banner, on color.status.danger.bg. Not the outline of an invalid field, which must reach 3:1: use color.status.danger.solid.

variables.name: color/status/warning/solid
variables.description: The filled background of a warning badge, banner or button for warnings that need attention but do not block. Not for warning text on a neutral background: use color.status.warning.fg.

variables.name: color/status/warning/solid-hover
variables.description: color.status.warning.solid while hovered. Not a resting colour.

variables.name: color/status/warning/solid-fg
variables.description: Text and icons on color.status.warning.solid and its hover colour. It is the ramp's own contrast colour, so it is white or dark ink as that solid needs. Not on a tinted status background: use the status fg. Not color.fg.on-accent, which belongs to the accent ramp.

variables.name: color/status/warning/fg
variables.description: Text and icons for warnings that need attention but do not block, on neutral backgrounds or on color.status.warning.bg. Not the only signal: pair it with an icon or text, colour alone does not carry meaning.

variables.name: color/status/warning/bg
variables.description: A tinted background for warnings that need attention but do not block: alerts, badges, inline messages. Not for filled buttons: use the status solid.

variables.name: color/status/warning/border
variables.description: The outline of a warning alert or banner, on color.status.warning.bg. Not the outline of an invalid field, which must reach 3:1: use color.status.danger.solid.

variables.name: color/status/success/solid
variables.description: The filled background of a success badge, banner or button for success and completion. Not for success text on a neutral background: use color.status.success.fg.

variables.name: color/status/success/solid-hover
variables.description: color.status.success.solid while hovered. Not a resting colour.

variables.name: color/status/success/solid-fg
variables.description: Text and icons on color.status.success.solid and its hover colour. It is the ramp's own contrast colour, so it is white or dark ink as that solid needs. Not on a tinted status background: use the status fg. Not color.fg.on-accent, which belongs to the accent ramp.

variables.name: color/status/success/fg
variables.description: Text and icons for success and completion, on neutral backgrounds or on color.status.success.bg. Not the only signal: pair it with an icon or text, colour alone does not carry meaning.

variables.name: color/status/success/bg
variables.description: A tinted background for success and completion: alerts, badges, inline messages. Not for filled buttons: use the status solid.

variables.name: color/status/success/border
variables.description: The outline of a success alert or banner, on color.status.success.bg. Not the outline of an invalid field, which must reach 3:1: use color.status.danger.solid.

variables.name: color/status/info/solid
variables.description: The filled background of a info badge, banner or button for neutral information. Not for info text on a neutral background: use color.status.info.fg.

variables.name: color/status/info/solid-hover
variables.description: color.status.info.solid while hovered. Not a resting colour.

variables.name: color/status/info/solid-fg
variables.description: Text and icons on color.status.info.solid and its hover colour. It is the ramp's own contrast colour, so it is white or dark ink as that solid needs. Not on a tinted status background: use the status fg. Not color.fg.on-accent, which belongs to the accent ramp.

variables.name: color/status/info/fg
variables.description: Text and icons for neutral information, on neutral backgrounds or on color.status.info.bg. Not the only signal: pair it with an icon or text, colour alone does not carry meaning.

variables.name: color/status/info/bg
variables.description: A tinted background for neutral information: alerts, badges, inline messages. Not for filled buttons: use the status solid.

variables.name: color/status/info/border
variables.description: The outline of a info alert or banner, on color.status.info.bg. Not the outline of an invalid field, which must reach 3:1: use color.status.danger.solid.

variables.name: elevation/flat/border
variables.description: Hairline border of the flat elevation: in dark themes it carries most of the separation. Cards, panels and table bodies that sit on the canvas without a lift. Use the three tokens of the role together (shadow, border, bg). Not for anything that floats above other content.

variables.name: elevation/flat/bg
variables.description: Surface colour of the flat elevation. Cards, panels and table bodies that sit on the canvas without a lift. Use the three tokens of the role together (shadow, border, bg). Not for anything that floats above other content.

variables.name: elevation/raised/border
variables.description: Hairline border of the raised elevation: in dark themes it carries most of the separation. Content one step above its surroundings: buttons, hovered cards, sticky bars. Use the three tokens of the role together (shadow, border, bg). Not for popovers and menus: use elevation.overlay.

variables.name: elevation/raised/bg
variables.description: Surface colour of the raised elevation. Content one step above its surroundings: buttons, hovered cards, sticky bars. Use the three tokens of the role together (shadow, border, bg). Not for popovers and menus: use elevation.overlay.

variables.name: elevation/overlay/border
variables.description: Hairline border of the overlay elevation: in dark themes it carries most of the separation. Layers that float above the page and close on an outside click: popovers, dropdown menus, tooltips, the command palette. Use the three tokens of the role together (shadow, border, bg). Not for dialogs that block the page: use elevation.modal.

variables.name: elevation/overlay/bg
variables.description: Surface colour of the overlay elevation. Layers that float above the page and close on an outside click: popovers, dropdown menus, tooltips, the command palette. Use the three tokens of the role together (shadow, border, bg). Not for dialogs that block the page: use elevation.modal.

variables.name: elevation/modal/border
variables.description: Hairline border of the modal elevation: in dark themes it carries most of the separation. The top layer, over a scrim: dialogs, alert dialogs, drawers and sheets. Use the three tokens of the role together (shadow, border, bg). Not for anything that does not block the page.

variables.name: elevation/modal/bg
variables.description: Surface colour of the modal elevation. The top layer, over a scrim: dialogs, alert dialogs, drawers and sheets. Use the three tokens of the role together (shadow, border, bg). Not for anything that does not block the page.

variables.name: ring/color
variables.description: Colour of the focus ring: outline: var(--by-ring-width) solid var(--by-ring-color). Not a selection or accent colour: use color.interactive.selected or color.accent.bg.

variables.name: syntax/keyword
variables.description: Editor text colour for keywords: SELECT, FROM, function, return. Monaco gets it as a hex value in the generated theme; CodeMirror reads the variable. Not for interface text outside a code editor: use color.fg.* or text status colours.

variables.name: syntax/string
variables.description: Editor text colour for string and character literals. Monaco gets it as a hex value in the generated theme; CodeMirror reads the variable. Not for interface text outside a code editor: use color.fg.* or text status colours.

variables.name: syntax/number
variables.description: Editor text colour for numeric literals. Monaco gets it as a hex value in the generated theme; CodeMirror reads the variable. Not for interface text outside a code editor: use color.fg.* or text status colours.

variables.name: syntax/comment
variables.description: Editor text colour for comments: they recede, but stay readable. Monaco gets it as a hex value in the generated theme; CodeMirror reads the variable. Not for interface text outside a code editor: use color.fg.* or text status colours.

variables.name: syntax/function
variables.description: Editor text colour for function and method names, and calls. Monaco gets it as a hex value in the generated theme; CodeMirror reads the variable. Not for interface text outside a code editor: use color.fg.* or text status colours.

variables.name: syntax/operator
variables.description: Editor text colour for operators and punctuation: = + , ;. Monaco gets it as a hex value in the generated theme; CodeMirror reads the variable. Not for interface text outside a code editor: use color.fg.* or text status colours.

variables.name: syntax/type
variables.description: Editor text colour for type names and built-in types: INTEGER, text, string. Monaco gets it as a hex value in the generated theme; CodeMirror reads the variable. Not for interface text outside a code editor: use color.fg.* or text status colours.

variables.name: syntax/identifier
variables.description: Editor text colour for table, column and variable names. Monaco gets it as a hex value in the generated theme; CodeMirror reads the variable. Not for interface text outside a code editor: use color.fg.* or text status colours.

variables.name: syntax/constant
variables.description: Editor text colour for constants and special values: TRUE, NULL, CURRENT_DATE. Monaco gets it as a hex value in the generated theme; CodeMirror reads the variable. Not for interface text outside a code editor: use color.fg.* or text status colours.

variables.name: syntax/error
variables.description: Editor text colour for syntax errors and invalid tokens. Monaco gets it as a hex value in the generated theme; CodeMirror reads the variable. Not for interface text outside a code editor: use color.fg.* or text status colours.

variables.name: editor/bg
variables.description: Background of a code editor and of a code block. Not for the app background: use color.bg.canvas.

variables.name: editor/fg
variables.description: Default text colour inside a code editor, for text that has no syntax role. Not for syntax-highlighted tokens: use syntax.*.

variables.name: editor/selection
variables.description: Background of selected text in a code editor (translucent, so the syntax colours stay readable). Not for a selected row or item: use color.interactive.selected.

variables.name: editor/line-highlight
variables.description: Background of the line the cursor is on (translucent). Not for hover: use color.interactive.hover.

variables.name: editor/cursor
variables.description: The text cursor (caret) of a code editor. Not for the focus ring: use color.ring.

variables.name: editor/gutter
variables.description: Colour of the line numbers in the gutter of a code editor (text, not the gutter background, which is editor.bg). Not for other secondary text: use color.fg.muted.

variables.name: editor/match
variables.description: Background behind search matches and the bracket that pairs with the one under the cursor (translucent). Not for the selection: use editor.selection.

variables.name: data/type/integer
variables.description: Colour of integer columns and values: cell text, type badges and column icons. Not the only cue for a type: pair it with the type name or an icon, colour alone does not carry meaning.

variables.name: data/type/decimal
variables.description: Colour of decimal, float and numeric columns and values: cell text, type badges and column icons. Not the only cue for a type: pair it with the type name or an icon, colour alone does not carry meaning.

variables.name: data/type/text
variables.description: Colour of text, varchar and char columns and values: cell text, type badges and column icons. Not the only cue for a type: pair it with the type name or an icon, colour alone does not carry meaning.

variables.name: data/type/boolean
variables.description: Colour of boolean columns and values: cell text, type badges and column icons. Not the only cue for a type: pair it with the type name or an icon, colour alone does not carry meaning.

variables.name: data/type/datetime
variables.description: Colour of date, time, timestamp and interval columns and values: cell text, type badges and column icons. Not the only cue for a type: pair it with the type name or an icon, colour alone does not carry meaning.

variables.name: data/type/json
variables.description: Colour of json and jsonb columns and values: cell text, type badges and column icons. Not the only cue for a type: pair it with the type name or an icon, colour alone does not carry meaning.

variables.name: data/type/binary
variables.description: Colour of bytea and blob columns and values: cell text, type badges and column icons. Not the only cue for a type: pair it with the type name or an icon, colour alone does not carry meaning.

variables.name: data/type/uuid
variables.description: Colour of uuid columns and values: cell text, type badges and column icons. Not the only cue for a type: pair it with the type name or an icon, colour alone does not carry meaning.

variables.name: data/null
variables.description: Colour of NULL and of an empty value in a cell: it recedes without disappearing. Not for the text of an empty string, which is a value: use color.fg.default.

variables.name: grid/header-bg
variables.description: Background of the header row of a result grid. Not for body rows: use grid.row-bg.

variables.name: grid/row-bg
variables.description: Background of a body row of a result grid. Not for alternate rows: use grid.row-bg-alt.

variables.name: grid/row-bg-alt
variables.description: Background of every other row when the grid is striped. Not for hover: use grid.row-hover.

variables.name: grid/row-hover
variables.description: Wash over the row under the pointer (translucent). Not for a selected row: use grid.selection-bg.

variables.name: grid/cell-border
variables.description: The hairlines between cells and rows. Not the outline of the selected cell: use grid.selection-border.

variables.name: grid/selection-bg
variables.description: Wash over selected cells and rows (translucent). Not for hover: use grid.row-hover.

variables.name: grid/selection-border
variables.description: The outline of the active cell and of a selected range. Not a cell separator: use grid.cell-border.

variables.name: grid/null-fg
variables.description: Text colour of NULL in a grid cell. Not for other muted text: use color.fg.muted.

variables.name: diff/add/bg
variables.description: Background of added lines and characters in a diff (translucent, so the syntax colours on top stay readable). Not for status messages: use color.status.*.bg. Pair it with diff.add.fg, a +/- marker or an icon.

variables.name: diff/add/fg
variables.description: Text and marker colour for added lines and characters in a diff: the +/- sign, line numbers and a summary count. Not for the code itself, which keeps its syntax colours.

variables.name: diff/remove/bg
variables.description: Background of removed lines and characters in a diff (translucent, so the syntax colours on top stay readable). Not for status messages: use color.status.*.bg. Pair it with diff.remove.fg, a +/- marker or an icon.

variables.name: diff/remove/fg
variables.description: Text and marker colour for removed lines and characters in a diff: the +/- sign, line numbers and a summary count. Not for the code itself, which keeps its syntax colours.

variables.name: diff/change/bg

variables.name: diff/change/fg
variables.description: Text and marker colour for changed lines and characters in a diff: the +/- sign, line numbers and a summary count. Not for the code itself, which keeps its syntax colours.

variables.name: size/control/xs
variables.description: Height of the smallest controls: inline tags, icon buttons inside a row. Not a touch target; not for primary actions.

variables.name: size/control/sm
variables.description: Height of small controls and of dense rows (toolbars, grid rows). Not for forms a user fills in at length: use size.control.md.

variables.name: size/control/md
variables.description: Height of standard controls: buttons, inputs, selects. Not a fixed pixel value: never hard-code 36px, the density mode changes it.

variables.name: size/control/lg
variables.description: Height of large controls: the main call to action, touch-first layouts. Not inside dense tools such as grids and toolbars.

variables.name: space/control/x
variables.description: Horizontal padding inside a standard control. Not for gaps between controls or for layout spacing.

variables.name: space/inline/xs
variables.description: The space between things on one line: an icon and its label, a badge and its text, buttons in a button group. Step xs: space.1 in comfortable density, space.0-5 in compact. Not for the gap between components in a row or grid (use space.gap.*) or for padding inside a container (use space.inset.*). Not a fixed pixel value: the density mode changes it.

variables.name: space/inline/sm
variables.description: The space between things on one line: an icon and its label, a badge and its text, buttons in a button group. Step sm: space.1-5 in comfortable density, space.1 in compact.
